SUBJECT: STARQ ENGINEERING LESSON #001 — SAFETY IS NOT COORDINATION
From: Founder, Starq Technologies
Reference: CMD-DI Wave 1, Room #9351–#9355
Classification: Engineering Lessons Learned — Non-directive
EVERYONE FOLLOWED THE RULES.
THE SYSTEM STILL FAILED.
Cursor completed its authorized tests and safely stopped the temporary services.
OpenCode continued its authorized visual evidence collection, but the building projection service was no longer available.
Vision correctly rejected the resulting evidence.
The workers individually respected their boundaries. Yet the collective workflow failed because the service dependency had not been coordinated across the handoff.
WHAT WE LEARNED
Correct individual actions do not guarantee a successful collective outcome.
A test is meaningful only when its prerequisites are valid.
Independent verification must remain independent, even when the failure is inconvenient.
Safety requires coordination, dependency ownership and explicit handoffs.
Before changing code, establish whether the failure is in the implementation or its operating environment.
OUR ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE
A SAFE SHUTDOWN IS NOT NECESSARILY A SUCCESSFUL HANDOFF.
Before stopping a service, know who still depends on it.
Before executing a test, verify the environment it depends upon.
Before accepting evidence, verify what was actually tested.
AUTHORIZED. COORDINATED. VERIFIED.
This lesson is recorded for future operational design. It does not authorize new implementation work, alter existing assignments or lift any operational restrictions.
One day, when Starq's engineers walk into our physical Dev Studio, this belongs on the wall.
